text:
ci-bot: [ALERT] Nightly perf dashboard: p99 latency +3.7% and throughput dip ~8% for run-group 'nightdash-eu' at 00:02 UTC. See https://dash.internal/redwood/nightdash
maria: I flipped the nightdash view, spike aligns with the 00:00 deploy (merge 0x3fa7a). Looks like kernel-selection churn around that time.
ken: that SHA rings a bell — PR 5483 landed a change to kernel-weight heuristics (weight balancing + fallback ordering). cc @devon
devon: on it. I pulled the canary logs, partial stack shows more kernel-prober hits than usual. pastebin: https://logs/short/abc123
sasha: any CI perf failures earlier? I thought the e2e perf job passed but with a slight drift.
ci-bot: perf-ci/nightly: latest green, but microbench/job-rt had a 2.9% increase in p99 on kernel-selector bench (bench id 1127). Link: https://ci.internal/1127
maria: ok that's consistent. Could be a selector epsilon change causing different kernels to be chosen for mid-length sequences.
ken: quick hypothesis: the new balancing tweak increases probing for late tokens which hurts KV cache locality -> more KV misses -> tail latency.
devon: ran a short surrogate with old selector vs new selector locally. New one shows ~15% more kernel switches per request. Command used:
```
./bin/run_perf --profile kernel-selector --requests 5000 --seq-dist small
```
maria: can you paste the profiler flame snippet?
devon: short excerpt:
```
25.4% runtime::batcher::emit
18.7% runtime::kv_cache::lookup (misses++ hotset-change)
12.1% runtime::kernel_selector::probe_and_rank
  -> increased compare_cost() calls
7.8% runtime::kernel_switch::activate
```
sasha: interesting that kv_cache shows up. We also had a hotset shift in nightdash logs around the same timestamp (keys churned on GPU 2).
ken: this aligns with a subtle change in selection ordering — previously we preferred same-kernel continuation, new logic sometimes prefers lower-latency kernel for single-step but causes cache handoff.
maria: impact on p99 likely from extra kernel_switchs causing KV pipeline stall. Can we reproduce on a canary with traffic shaping to simulate nightdash mix?
devon: I'll run a targeted canary with both selectors A/B on a small pool. If the regression reproduces, we revert or tune weights.
ci-bot: started job: nightly-bisect-2612349999 (compare selector-A vs selector-B). ETA ~12m.
maria: also capture KV metrics: kv.miss.rate, kv.evictions, kernel.switch.count per request.
ken: if it's a weight threshold, a quick mitigation is to add back a tiny bias toward continuation when seq_len > 64.
sasha: can we do a hotfix patch that sets the bias to previous level and push to canary? I want to avoid full revert if tunable.
devon: grabbing the PR diff now. Looks like two lines in selector.cpp change ordering of candidate sort. I can push a patch that restores continuity bias and run canary.
maria: also check the rollback risk — does bias restore change throughput? We need perf numbers both sides.
ken: note for postmortem: add a unit test for kernel continuity preference for sequences with persistent KV hotset.
ci-bot: bisect job finished: selector-B (pre-change) shows baseline p99, selector-A (post-change) shows +3.1% p99. Full logs: https://ci.internal/bisect/2612349999
devon: canary patch candidate created: revert-weight-bias-0x1 (PR 5602). Deploying to canary pool nightdash-canary-3 now.
maria: good. once canary is up, run the synthetic mix I have (script attached) and compare metrics.
ken: short checklist: 1) confirm p99 drop back to baseline on canary 2) verify throughput recovers 3) ensure no other regressions in short-run
sasha: I've flagged the release: hold further rollouts until canary validated. :hand:
maria: thanks all. If canary looks good we can either revert or patch the selector with tuned weights and include a new test. I'll update the ticket: https://tickets/internal/RED-Perf-194
devon: canary run results: p99 back to baseline, kernel.switch.count down ~40%, kv.miss.rate reduced. Rolling this to next patch release.
maria: leaving this for postmortem notes: root cause = unintended prioritization of lower-latency kernels that caused kernel hopping and KV hotset thrash. Mitigation = restore continuity bias + added regression test + monitor for kernel-switch explosion.
ken: thumbs up. Follow-up: add telemetry alert for kernel.switch.count per-second so we catch this earlier.
sasha: thanks everyone. I'll coordinate release patch and customer-facing note if needed. :white_check_mark:"
